t.1.61.2: I wish to hear truly, and in due order, of the birth and deeds among men of these great-souled beings.
t.1.61.1: Janamejaya said: Of the Devas and the Dānavas, of the Yakṣas and the Rakṣases, and indeed of all other beings, O blessed one, I...
t.1.61.4: He who was the bull among Dānavas, known as Vipracitti, became the bull among men known as Jarāsaṃdha.
t.1.61.5: But that son of Diti, O king, who is remembered as Hiraṇyakaśipu, was born in the world of men as Śiśupāla, a bull among men.
t.1.61.3: O lord of men, those dwellers of heaven who were born among humans, and first of all the Dānavas as well, all of them I shall now describe in full.
t.1.61.6: He who was the younger brother of Prahrāda, renowned as Saṃhrāda, was born as the bull among the Vāhlīkas, renowned as Śalya.
t.1.61.7: But the splendid Anuhrāda, who was known as the youngest-born, became a lord of men renowned as Dhṛṣṭaketu.
t.1.61.8: But the Daitya who was celebrated by the name of Śibi, O king, became a king on earth renowned as Druma.
t.1.61.9: He who among them was the foremost of asuras, Bāṣkala by name, became the lord of men renowned as Bhagadatta.
t.1.61.11: These five mighty great asuras, O king, were born among the Kekayas as high-souled men, the very best of the bulls among kings.
t.1.61.10: Ayaḥśiras, Aśvaśiras, and the mighty Ayaḥśaṅku, and likewise Gaganamūrdhan, and Vegavat here as the fifth.
t.1.61.13: But the glorious great Asura who was renowned as Svarbhānu became the king of men known as Ugrasena, a doer of fierce deeds.
t.1.61.12: The next one, the valiant one renowned as Ketumān, became a king on earth known as Amitaujas.
t.1.61.14: But the glorious great Asura who was renowned as Aśva became a king named Aśoka, of great vigor and valor.
t.1.61.15: But the one who was his younger brother, O king, known as Aśvapati, that Daiteya became King Hārdikya, a bull among men.
t.1.61.16: But that glorious great Asura who was renowned as Vṛṣaparvan became a king on earth, known as Dīrghaprajña.
t.1.61.17: But Ajaka, O king, who was the younger brother of Vṛṣaparvan, became a king on earth renowned by the name Malla.
t.1.61.18: The mighty asura who was known as Aśvagrīva, endowed with great strength, became on earth the king known as Rocamāna.
t.1.61.20: He who was the foremost of asuras, renowned by the name Tuhuṇḍa, became the king known as Senābindu.
t.1.61.19: But the wise Sūkṣma, O king, who was proclaimed glorious, was on earth the king renowned as Bṛhanta.
t.1.61.21: He who was named Isṛpā, foremost in strength among those Asuras, became on earth a king named Pāpajit, renowned for his valour.
t.1.61.22: But the great Asura who was known as Ekacakra became renowned on earth, known as Prativindhya.
t.1.61.23: But Virūpākṣa, the son of Diti, a great Asura and a wondrous fighter, was the king on earth renowned as Citravarman.
t.1.61.24: But the heroic Hara, foremost of the Dānavas and destroyer of his foes, was born as a bull among men, renowned as Suvāstu.
t.1.61.25: But Ahara, of great splendor, the destroyer of the ranks of his enemies, became the king named Bāhlīka, renowned upon the earth.
t.1.61.27: But Nikumbha, unconquered in battle and of great intelligence, was born on earth as an excellent lord of the land, remembered by the name Devādhipa.
t.1.61.28: That great Asura named Śarabha, who was among those Daiteyas, was born here among men as the royal sage named Paurava.
t.1.61.26: The moon-faced Nicandra, who was the foremost of the asuras, became the illustrious king known as Muñjakeśa.
t.1.61.30: Candra, the foremost of the sons of Diti, who was like the lord of the stars in the world, was born as the royal sage named Ṛṣika, the best of kings.
t.1.61.29: He who was Śalabha, the second among those Asuras, became the Bāhlīka king of men named Prahrāda.
t.1.61.31: He who was the foremost of the Asuras, renowned by the name Mṛtapā, know him, O best of kings, to be the king Paścimānūpaka.
t.1.61.32: But the greatly splendid one, renowned as the great Asura Gaviṣṭha, became a king on earth known as Drumasena.
t.1.61.33: But the glorious great Asura who was known as Mayūra became a lord of the earth renowned as Viśva.
t.1.61.35: The asura who was renowned as Candrahantṛ, the foremost among them, became the royal sage named Śunaka, a lord of men.
t.1.61.36: But the great Asura who was known as Vināśana of Candra became the royal sage named Jānaki, a lord of men.
t.1.61.34: He who was renowned as Suparṇa, the younger brother of that one, became a king on earth known as Kālakīrti.
t.1.61.37: And he who was named Dīrghajihva, O Kauravya, the bull among the Dānavas, became the lord of the earth renowned on earth as the King of Kāśi.
t.1.61.38: But that Graha, the crusher of the moon and the sun, whom Siṃhī bore, became a lord of men renowned as Krātha.
t.1.61.39: Of the four sons of Anāyus, the foremost was the asura named Vikṣara, full of splendour; he became the king Vasumitra.
t.1.61.41: But that foremost of asuras who was known as Balavīra became the king known as Pauṇḍramatsyaka.
t.1.61.42: But the great Asura who was widely renowned as Vṛtra, O king, became the royal sage named Maṇimān, a ruler of men.
t.1.61.40: The second, O lord of men, the great asura Vikṣarādya, became the king renowned as the lord of Pāṃsurāṣṭra.
t.1.61.43: The Asura who was his younger brother, known as Krodhahantṛ, became renowned on earth as Daṇḍa; he was a king.
t.1.61.44: And that other one, who was proclaimed by the name Krodhavardhana, became a lord of men renowned as Daṇḍadhāra.
t.1.61.45: As for the sons of Kālakā, eight of them were born as kings of men, O tiger among kings, and their valour was equal to that of tigers.
t.1.61.46: The great asura who was foremost among those eight Kāleyas became the illustrious king Jayatsena among the Magadhas.
t.1.61.48: But the third great Asura, O great king, mighty-armed and of terrible prowess, was born on earth as the lord of the Niṣādas.
t.1.61.47: Then the second of them, glorious and like Indra of the tawny steeds, became the king known as Aparājita.
t.1.61.49: But the one among them who is proclaimed as the fourth became renowned on earth as Śreṇimān, the best of royal seers.
t.1.61.50: The fifth of them, the great Asura who was foremost among them, was born here as the scorcher of foes renowned by the name Mahaujas.
t.1.61.51: But the sixth among them, the wise one who was a great Asura, became renowned on earth as Abhīru, the best of royal sages.
t.1.61.52: And from that very host of theirs was born King Samudrasena, renowned throughout the sea-bounded earth, a knower of the true essence of dharma and artha.
t.1.61.53: The eighth of those Kāleyas, O king, was the scorcher of foes named Bṛhant, righteous in spirit and devoted to the welfare of all beings.
t.1.61.54: The host named Krodhavaśa, which was described to you, O king, from it were born heroic lords of men here on earth.
t.1.61.55: Nandika and Karṇaveṣṭa, Siddhārtha and likewise Kīṭaka, Suvīra and Subāhu, Mahāvīra and then Bāhlika.
t.1.61.56: Krodha, Vicitya, Surasa, the glorious king Nīla, and Vīradhāman, O Kauravya, and one Bhūmipāla by name.
t.1.61.58: Āṣāḍha and Vāyuvega, and likewise Bhūritejas, Ekalavya and Sumitra, Vāṭadhāna and also Gomukha.
t.1.61.57: There was one named Dantavaktra, and one called by name Durjaya, and Rukmī, a tiger among kings, and King Janamejaya.
t.1.61.59: And the Kārūṣaka kings, and likewise Kṣemadhūrti, Śrutāyus and Uddhava, and likewise Bṛhatsena.
t.1.61.61: Thus, O great king, from the host called Krodhavaśa there arose of old upon the earth a multitude of kings, of great fame and great strength.
t.1.61.60: Kṣemogratīrtha, Kuhara the lord of men among the Kaliṅgas, and the wise ruler of men renowned as Īśvara.
t.1.61.62: But the king of men named Devaka, whose splendor equaled that of the king of the gods, was born on earth from the foremost lord of the Gandharvas.
t.1.61.63: Know, O Bhārata, that Droṇa Bhāradvāja, who was not born from a womb, arose from a portion of Bṛhaspati, the divine sage of great renown.
t.1.61.64: He who, O tiger among kings, was the foremost of bowmen and the best knower of all weapons, of vast fame and great splendor, was born here among men.
t.1.61.65: He was Droṇa, whom those who know the Veda know as the foremost in the science of archery and in the Veda, a man of Indra-like deeds and the increaser of his own lineage.
t.1.61.67: Aśvatthāman of great valor, the destroyer of the ranks of his enemies, a hero with eyes like lotus petals, was born upon the earth, O lord of men.
t.1.61.66: And from Mahādeva and Antaka, and from Kāma and Krodha, united into one, O Bhārata, there was born a hero, a scorcher of foes.
t.1.61.68: The eight Vasus were born in Gaṅgā as the sons of Śaṃtanu, through the curse of Vasiṣṭha and by the command of Vāsava.
t.1.61.69: The youngest of them was Bhīṣma, who made the Kurus fearless; wise, versed in the Veda, eloquent, he brought destruction upon the ranks of his enemies.
t.1.61.70: He, the most excellent of all the learned, of great splendor, who fought with the great-souled Rāma Jāmadagnya, the Bhārgava.
t.1.61.71: But he, O king, who was born on earth as the brahmarṣi named Kṛpa, know him to be of surpassing manly prowess, sprung from the host of the Rudras.
t.1.61.72: But he who was the king in the world named Śakuni, a great chariot-warrior, know him, O king, to be Dvāpara born, the crusher of foes.
t.1.61.73: But Sātyaki, true to his word, he who is the upholder of the Vṛṣṇi clan, the crusher of foes, was born from a portion of the gods, the Maruts.
t.1.61.75: And next, O king, know that the lord of men Kṛtavarman was born, a man of matchless deeds, the very best among bulls of the kṣatriyas.
t.1.61.74: And the royal sage Drupada, best of all bearers of weapons, was also born from that very same host into this world of men, O king.
t.1.61.76: Know that the royal sage named Virāṭa, crusher of foes and tormentor of enemy kingdoms, was born from the host of the Maruts.
t.1.61.77: The son of Ariṣṭā, the lord of the Gandharvas renowned as Haṃsa, was born as the increaser of the Kuru lineage.
t.1.61.78: And from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana too was born the one known as Dhṛtarāṣṭra, long-armed and of great splendor, a lord of men whose eyes were his wisdom; through his mother's fault and the seer's anger he was born blind.
t.1.61.79: Know that Vidura, born in this world, the best of the intelligent, was the most fortunate son of Atri, the best of those who have sons.
t.1.61.80: But from a portion of Kali was born on earth King Duryodhana, evil-minded and wicked of thought, the bringer of disgrace to the Kurus.
t.1.61.81: He who was the Kali-man, hated by the whole world, that lowest of men who caused the entire earth to be slaughtered, by whom a great enmity was kindled that brought about the destruction of beings.
t.1.61.82: All the brothers descended from Pulastya were born here among men: the hundred, Duḥśāsana and the rest, all of them doers of cruel deeds.
t.1.61.84: Know, O king, that King Yudhiṣṭhira was a portion of Dharma, Bhīmasena of the Wind, and Arjuna of the king of the gods.
t.1.61.83: Durmukha and Duḥsaha, and the others who have not been named, those companions of Duryodhana were all Paulastyas, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.61.86: The mighty son of Soma who was known as Suvarcas became Abhimanyu of great fame, the son of Arjuna.
t.1.61.85: Likewise, the two portions of the Aśvins, unequalled in beauty on earth, were Nakula and Sahadeva, who captivated the hearts of all the world.
t.1.61.87: Know Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great chariot-warrior, to be a portion of Agni; and know Śikhaṇḍin, O king, who was both woman and man, to be a Rākṣasa.
t.1.61.88: And the five who were born as the sons of Draupadī, O bull of the Bharatas, know them, O king, to be the hosts of the Viśvedevas, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.61.89: Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior, who was born wearing armor, know him to be the unsurpassed portion of the god Divākara, the Sun.
t.1.61.90: He who is called Nārāyaṇa, the eternal god of gods, a portion of him was among men: the mighty Vāsudeva.
t.1.61.91: Mighty Baladeva was a portion of the serpent Śeṣa. Know, O king, that the greatly energetic Pradyumna was Sanatkumāra.
t.1.61.92: Thus, O lord of men, many other portions of the heaven-dwellers were born in the family of Vasudeva, increasing the family's prosperity.
t.1.61.93: And that host of Apsarases which I have described to you, O king, a portion of it was born on earth at the command of Vāsava.
t.1.61.95: A portion of Śrī was born on the face of the earth for the sake of love, in the family of Drupada, as a blameless maiden arising from the middle of the sacrificial altar.
t.1.61.94: Those sixteen thousand goddesses, O lord of men, were born in the world of men and became the wives of Nārāyaṇa.
t.1.61.96: She was neither too short nor too tall, fragrant as the blue lotus, with long eyes like lotus petals, lovely hips, and long black hair.
t.1.61.97: Endowed with all auspicious marks and lustrous like a beryl gem, she in private ravished the hearts of the five lords of men.
t.1.61.98: The two goddesses Siddhi and Dhṛti were born as Kuntī and Mādrī, the mothers of the five; and Mati was born as the daughter of Subala.
t.1.61.99: Thus, O king, the descent by partial incarnation of the gods and Asuras, likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases, and of the Rākṣasas, has been recounted to you.
t.1.61.100: Those kings, mad for battle, who arose upon the earth, and those great-souled ones who were born in the vast lineage of the Yadus,
t.1.61.101: This account of the descent of the partial incarnations, which brings wealth, fame, sons, long life and victory, should be heard by one who is free from envy.
t.1.61.102: Having heard of the descent by partial incarnation of the gods, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas, the wise man, knowing the origin and the dissolution of beings, does not lose heart in times of hardship.
